0.long_answer: Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (UPPP) is a surgery frequently performed to treat both chronic tonsillitis and obstructive sleep apnea. The procedure involves removal or remodeling of tissues in the throat such as the soft palate, uvula, and tonsils, with the aim of widening the airway to prevent blockages during sleep. A known complication of UPPP is dysgeusia, which refers to an alteration in taste sensation. This change can occur due to nerve injury or other modifications of the oral structures during the surgical procedure.
